In [[probability theory]], a '''nearly completely decomposable (NCD) Markov chain''' is a [[Markov chain]] where the state space can be partitioned in such a way that movement within a partition occurs much more frequently than movement between partitions.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Kontovasilis | first1 = K. P. | last2 = Mitrou | first2 = N. M. | title = Markov-Modulated Traffic with Nearly Complete Decomposability Characteristics and Associated Fluid Queueing Models | journal = Advances in Applied Probability | volume = 27 | issue = 4 | pages = 1144–1185 | doi = 10.2307/1427937 | year = 1995 | jstor = 1427937 | s2cid = 123810850 }}</ref> Particularly efficient algorithms exist to compute the [[stationary distribution]] of Markov chains with this property.<ref name="kms">{{Cite journal | last1 = Koury | first1 = J. R. | last2 = McAllister | first2 = D. F. | last3 = Stewart | first3 = W. J. | doi = 10.1137/0605019 | title = Iterative Methods for Computing Stationary Distributions of Nearly Completely Decomposable Markov Chains | journal = [[SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods]] | volume = 5 | issue = 2 | pages = 164–186 | year = 1984 }}</ref>

==Definition==

[[Albert Ando|Ando]] and [[Franklin M. Fisher|Fisher]] define a completely decomposable matrix as one where "an identical rearrangement of rows and columns leaves a set of square [[submatrices]] on the [[principal diagonal]] and zeros everywhere else." A nearly completely decomposable matrix is one where an identical rearrangement of rows and columns leaves a set of square submatrices on the principal diagonal and ''small nonzeros'' everywhere else.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Ando | first1 = A. | author-link1 = Albert Ando| last2 = Fisher | first2 = F. M. | author-link2 = Franklin M. Fisher| title = Near-Decomposability, Partition and Aggregation, and the Relevance of Stability Discussions | journal = International Economic Review | volume = 4 | issue = 1 | pages = 53–67 | doi = 10.2307/2525455 | year = 1963 | jstor = 2525455 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Courtois | first1 = P. J. | title = Error Analysis in Nearly-Completely Decomposable Stochastic Systems | journal = Econometrica | volume = 43 | issue = 4 | pages = 691–709 | doi = 10.2307/1913078 | year = 1975 | jstor = 1913078 }}</ref>

==Example==

A [[Markov chain]] with [[Stochastic matrix|transition matrix]]
::<math>P = 
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\
\frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\
0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\
\end{pmatrix} + \epsilon \begin{pmatrix}
-\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\
0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\
\frac{1}{2} & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\
0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} \\
\end{pmatrix}</math>
is nearly completely decomposable if ''ε'' is small (say 0.1).<ref>Example 1.1 from {{cite book|page=[https://archive.org/details/discretetimemark00ying_757/page/n21 8]|title=Discrete-time Markov chains: two-time-scale methods and applications|url=https://archive.org/details/discretetimemark00ying_757|url-access=limited|first1=George|last1=Yin|first2=Qing|last2=Zhang|publisher=Springer|year=2005|isbn= 978-0-387-21948-6}}</ref>

==Stationary distribution algorithms==

Special-purpose iterative algorithms have been designed for NCD Markov chains<ref name="kms" /> though the multi–level algorithm, a general purpose algorithm,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Horton | first1 = G. | last2 = Leutenegger | first2 = S. T. | doi = 10.1145/183019.183040 | title = A multi-level solution algorithm for steady-state Markov chains | journal = ACM SIGMETRICS Performance Evaluation Review | volume = 22 | pages = 191–200 | year = 1994 | s2cid = 1110664 }}</ref> has been shown experimentally to be competitive and in some cases significantly faster.<ref>{{cite tech report|title=On the Utility of the Multi-Level Algorithm for the Solution of Nearly Completely Decomposable Markov Chains (ICASE Report No. 94-44)|url=https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA284423.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130408131233/http://www.dtic.mil/cgi-bin/GetTRDoc?Location=U2&doc=GetTRDoc.pdf&AD=ADA284423|url-status=live|archive-date=April 8, 2013|last1=Leutenegger |first1=Scott T.|last2=Horton |first2=Graham |date=June 1994 |quote=We present experimental results indicating that the general- purpose Multi-Level algorithm is competitive, and can be significantly faster than the special-purpose KMS algorithm when Gauss-Seidel and Gaussian Elimination are used for solving the individual blocks. Markov chains, Multi- level, Numerical solution.|institution=NASA|id=Contractor Report 194929}}</ref>
